title: Hostinger Review 2026: Pricing, Plans and Renewal Costs
excerpt: Hostinger starts at $1.99 a month on a 48-month term and renews at $10.99. Here is what each plan includes, how fast it tested, how to set up WordPress and who should look elsewhere.

meta._yoast_wpseo_title: Hostinger Review 2026: Pricing, Plans and Renewal Costs
meta._yoast_wpseo_metadesc: Hostinger review for 2026: plans, first term and renewal prices, WordPress hosting, speed and support, plus who should skip it and how to set up a site.
meta.rl_answer: Hostinger is a fast, low-cost host for beginners and small WordPress sites. Premium is $1.99 a month on a 48-month term and renews at $10.99. Staging starts on Unlimited.
meta.rl_faqs:
Is Hostinger good for hosting? | Yes for beginners, blogs and small business sites. Independent tests measured server response between 227 and 447 ms and uptime between 99.96% and 100%. The trade-offs are the renewal price and no phone support.
How much does Hostinger hosting cost? | On Hostinger's pricing page on 20 November 2026, Premium was $1.99 a month, Unlimited $2.79 and Cloud Startup $7.99, all on a 48-month term paid upfront. Renewal is $10.99, $16.99 and $25.99 a month.
Does Hostinger cost more when you renew? | Yes. Premium renews at $10.99 a month, which is 5.5 times the $1.99 Black Friday price. Hostinger says each plan renews for the same term, so check the renewal terms in your account before the date.
Why is Hostinger so cheap? | The lowest price needs a long prepaid term, so you pay for four years at checkout. Hostinger also credits server optimization. After the first term the price rises.
Is Hostinger good for WordPress? | Yes. Every plan has one-click WordPress install, LiteSpeed Cache, automatic updates, WP-CLI and SSH. Staging, object cache and multisite start on Unlimited, so Premium users have no staging tool.
How many websites can I host on Hostinger Premium? | Premium allows 3 websites, 20 GB of SSD storage and 400,000 files. Unlimited and Cloud Startup allow unlimited websites, subject to Hostinger's Fair Usage Policy.
Does the Hostinger website builder include hosting? | Yes. Hostinger says its website builder is included in every hosting plan. It runs on AI credits that come as a one-time gift, and the Black Friday offer doubles them.
Does Hostinger have a money-back guarantee? | Yes. Hostinger lists a 30-day money-back guarantee on its plans. Check the refund policy for exclusions, such as the domain.
Is the free domain free after the first year? | No. The free domain covers the first year only. You must register it within 12 months of buying the plan, and then you pay the renewal price each year.
Does Hostinger have phone support? | No. Support is 24/7 live chat and email, according to WPBeginner and HostingTestLab. Chat starts with an AI assistant and moves to a person when needed.
Is Hostinger good for an online store? | It can run WooCommerce on any plan, but its own Ecommerce store builder starts on Unlimited. All About Cookies notes Hostinger is not PCI compliant, so use a payment provider that handles the card step.
Who should avoid Hostinger? | People who need phone support, want to pay month to month at the lowest price, take card payments directly on the site or need a dedicated server. Hostinger sells none.
Is Hostinger safe? | Hostinger lists a web application firewall, a malware scanner, DDoS protection with Cloudflare-protected nameservers, free SSL and a secure access manager. It is not PCI compliant, according to All About Cookies.
Which Hostinger plan should I choose? | Choose Premium for one small site and Unlimited if you want daily backups and staging. Pick Cloud Startup for steady traffic, an agency or a busier store.

meta.rl_takeaways:
Premium is $1.99 a month on a 48-month term and renews at $10.99 (Hostinger, 20 Nov 2026).
Five independent tests measured 227 to 447 ms server response and 99.96% to 100% uptime.
Staging, object cache and multisite are not on Premium. They start on Unlimited.
Over five years, Premium averages about $3.79 a month.
meta.rl_r_verdict: Hostinger is one of the strongest low-price starting points for a WordPress site. Independent tests show fast response and near-perfect uptime, and the sale price is hard to beat. Budget for the renewal, pick Unlimited if you want staging, and look elsewhere if you need phone support.
meta.rl_r_buy:
You are launching a WordPress blog, a portfolio or a small business site.
You want fast response and a very low first-term price.
You can commit for four years, or you will use the 30-day refund to try it first.
meta.rl_r_skip:
You need phone support or a person on every call.
You want the lowest price on a short term, or a dedicated server.
You take card payments directly on the site: All About Cookies says Hostinger is not PCI compliant.
meta.rl_r_pros:
Black Friday prices from $1.99 a month on a 48-month term.
227 to 447 ms server response and 99.96% to 100% uptime in independent tests.
One-click WordPress, LiteSpeed Cache, WP-CLI and SSH on every plan.
30-day money-back guarantee and free SSL.
Free domain for the first year and free migration for WordPress sites.
meta.rl_r_cons:
The sale price needs a 48-month prepayment.
Renewal is 3.3 to 6.1 times the offer price.
Premium has weekly backups and no staging.
No phone support, and chat starts with an AI assistant.
No dedicated servers.
meta.rl_r_best: Beginners, blogs and small business sites
meta.rl_r_method:
Our own use | Reinforce Lab uses Hostinger as its web host. We work in hPanel and over SSH, so we know the control panel and the setup first-hand. We did not benchmark it for this page, so every speed number here belongs to the team that measured it
Pricing and plan limits | Hostinger's pricing and Black Friday pages, read on 20 November 2026. We recorded each plan price, the term it needs, the renewal price, the limits and the WordPress features on each plan
Independent tests | Five published test sets: WPBeginner (July 2026), Gizmodo (September 2026), HostingTestLab (summary of five tests, updated 17 November 2026), All About Cookies (updated 9 November 2026) and TechRadar
Competitor reviews | The top-ranking Hostinger reviews read for structure and questions: WPBeginner, Gizmodo, HostingTestLab, Etemora, HereFlow and Website Planet
Questions people ask | The questions the top pages answer in their headings, plus the questions people search for in Semrush, such as how many sites Premium allows and whether the builder includes hosting
When sources disagree | We show both numbers and say which we used. For prices we used Hostinger's own page, because it is the one you pay
Our calculations | The renewal multiples and the five-year cost table are our own arithmetic from Hostinger's prices
Freshness | Prices and offers are read again before this page goes live, and the page carries the date they were checked
What we did not do | We did not run our own speed or uptime test. Each test number is credited to the team that measured it
